flashcard_questions.q: In which century did the blues originate?
Where in the United States did the blues originate?
flashcard_questions.a: In African American communities of the Deep South.
Any chord with more than three notes.

flashcard_questions.q: Which chord type appears on almost every chord of a 12-bar blues?
How is a dominant 7th chord built?
flashcard_questions.a: A major triad plus a flattened 7th note.

flashcard_questions.q: How is a major 7th chord built?
flashcard_questions.a: A major triad plus the natural 7th note.

flashcard_questions.q: Which degrees of the major scale are flattened to make blues notes?
How is the blues scale built?
flashcard_questions.a: The minor pentatonic scale with the flattened 5th added.

flashcard_questions.q: How many notes does the blues scale have?

flashcard_questions.a: Pairs of quavers played unevenly, the first longer than the second.
Creating music spontaneously during a performance, not from a written score.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the head in a jazz performance?
flashcard_questions.a: The main melody, played by the whole ensemble.

flashcard_questions.q: In Bessie Smith's blues recording, which two parts use call and response?
Which ensemble type plays on Miles Davis's So What?
Which string instrument is not common in traditional jazz and blues?

notes: 15 cards: 2 origin cards, 4 harmony cards (extended chords, dominant 7th, major 7th, blues notes), 2 blues-scale cards, 4 term-to-definition (swung rhythm, improvisation, the head, plus the violin misconception), and 2 example-to-feature cards on the named recordings (Bessie Smith call and response, Miles Davis sextet). Ensemble instrument lists were left out so no answer becomes an enumeration. Recordings are named as works, with no lyric quoted.
